key_insight: Femtosecond laser welding of fused silica to 6061 aluminum succeeds best when heat input is tightly controlled, with scanning speed, spacing, and fixture preload jointly governing crack formation and joint strength.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical process window for joining brittle/ductile dissimilar materials in high-reliability optics, aerospace, and MEMS assemblies.
method: Varied scanning speed, pulse energy, scanning spacing, and fixture preload during femtosecond laser welding.
Measured joint shear strength, microstructure, and elemental diffusion to link parameters with defect formation.
Optimized to 6 mm/s scanning speed, 140 µm spacing, and low preload to suppress macroscopic cracks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the optimized setting produced a high-strength joint with uniform elemental transition and no macroscopic cracks.
watch_item: The process appears highly sensitive to clamping conditions, so preload control and surface contact quality must be tightly managed for repeatable production.
paper_title: Process Parameter Optimization and Crack Formation Mechanism of Femtosecond Laser Welding of Fused Silica/6061 Aluminum Alloy
